It loads the aggregate through the OrderRepository port and asks the domain function canCancelOrder whether the order can be cancelled. It then has the Catalog domain service release stock for each item and saves the order through the port. The rule about whether an order may be cancelled lives in the domain, and the use case only acts on the answer. Looping over items to call catalog.release counts as coordination, not a business rule. The file contains no persistence code, no transport or HTTP handling, and no framework code. One thing to note: execute never sets the order's state to cancelled before saving. That looks like a correctness bug, but it doesn't put a responsibility in the wrong layer, so it is outside this rule.
